title: Article 31C — Saving of laws giving effect to certain Directive Principles

content.overview: Article 31C is a savings clause for laws giving effect to specified Directive Principles, protecting them against Articles 14 and 19 within the limits of the surviving constitutional text. Its drafting history includes the Twenty-fifth Amendment and later developments; Minerva Mills is a central authority on the balance between Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles. Verify the official text and the ratio of controlling cases before any advice on a particular statute.

sections.heading: Function
sections.body: Article 31C links certain Directive Principle-implementing laws to a limited immunity from Articles 14 and 19. The precise scope depends on the constitutional text as it stands and on Supreme Court decisions interpreting it.

sections.heading: Caution on current scope
sections.body: Do not expand or shrink Article 31C by informal paraphrase. Read the article as published in the official Constitution and the holdings of Minerva Mills and any later controlling authority relevant to the challenge. Case names here are orientation only.

sections.heading: Track B
sections.body: When a welfare statute is challenged under Articles 14 or 19, determine whether Article 31C is invoked, whether the statute gives effect to the relevant Directive Principle, and what the present constitutional text and case law allow. Record the statute's statement of objects and the Directive Principle cited.
